viewer_strategy.central_viewer_question: What are the most important AI developments from this week, and what do they mean in practice?
viewer_strategy.refined_viewer_promise: After watching, you’ll know what each update enables in practice. what autonomous coding agents can do in real projects, how Trusted Contact and Cybersecurity governance affect risk and deployment, what new voice-models in the API enable for real-time apps, and how to evaluate adoption with concrete checklists for governance, privacy, and integration. Every story is kept short and evidence-first — no hype, no padding.
viewer_payoff: understand what each update actually does
separate product launches from technical advances
know which changes affect developer tools and APIs
identify which updates require follow-up attention

hook_instruction.direction: Open with a rapid-fire roundup of the episode's eight topics (Codex safety, Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5.5/5.5-Cyber, new API voice models, Parloa service agents, Uber/OpenAI collaboration, Trusted Contact in ChatGPT, and ads testing). Then pivot to concise, practice-focused takeaways that answer: what autonomous coding agents can do in real projects, how Trusted Contact and cybersecurity governance affect deployment risk, and what the updated APIs and tooling enable for developers. End with the single most actionable takeaway for viewers to apply this week.
hook_instruction.why_it_works: The roundup format leverages multiple documented updates to deliver immediate, concrete value for developers while maintaining a steady pace that minimizes hype.

blocked_hook_angles.angle: Overpromising universal, immediate adoption of autonomous coding
blocked_hook_angles.reason: The episode presents updates, not a universal adoption timeline.

blocked_hook_angles.angle: Predicting a strict rollout timeline for Trusted Contact across ChatGPT
blocked_hook_angles.reason: Timeline details are not specified in the claims and would risk overclaim.

evidence_rules.cautious_language_rule: For any cautious_claim_id, use qualifying language: may, could, suggests, appears to. Do not assert certainty.

retention_beats.instruction: Tell viewers exactly what they will understand by the end of this episode.
